routine_specs.name: carvana_search_inventory
routine_specs.description: Search Carvana cars for sale by make/model/body style and filters; return vehicles with features, pricing, and VDP links.

routine_specs.name: carvana_get_vehicle_details
routine_specs.description: Get detailed Carvana vehicle data for a specific vehicleId including specs, features, pricing, and links.

experiments.hypothesis: Carvana search inventory data can be accessed via the public /cars SRP HTML by extracting structured Vehicle ld+json blocks, avoiding blocked apik.carvana.io APIs.
experiments.rationale: Network exploration shows Cloudflare blocks direct API calls to apik.carvana.io, but DOM exploration shows many application/ld+json[data-qa=vehicle-ld] blobs on SRP pages that contain VIN, price, mileage, and VDP URLs. If these are still present live, we can build a search routine that uses UI navigation + HTML/JS extraction instead of direct APIs.
experiments.prompt:
Goal: Determine if we can reliably search Carvana inventory by keyword/filters using the public SRP UI and extract rich vehicle data (features, price, links) from structured data, without calling blocked APIs.

Steps (use tools by name):
1) Use browser_navigate to go to https://www.carvana.com/cars.
2) Use browser_get_dom to confirm there is a search input with name="search" and filter facets similar to those described in the exploration (make, model, colors, driveTypes, ways-to-save, etc.). Capture the relevant selectors.
3) In the search box, use browser_eval_js to focus and type a query like "audi" and press Enter (or click the search button) to trigger search. You can also use browser_eval_js to set the input value and dispatch an Enter key event.
4) After results load, use browser_get_dom to verify that vehicle tiles are rendered and that there are application/ld+json[data-qa="vehicle-ld"] script tags in the page.
5) Use browser_eval_js to collect and JSON.parse all application/ld+json[data-qa="vehicle-ld"] scripts into an array of Vehicle objects. Return a sample of at least 5 vehicles with fields: name, modelDate, vehicleIdentificationNumber, sku, mileageFromOdometer, offers.price, offers.priceCurrency, and url.
6) Also, inspect whether any additional filter state (make, model, body style, color, drivetrain, fuel type, free delivery) is encoded in the URL query parameters (e.g., /cars/filters?...) or in data attributes / JS globals. Report what you find.

Output:
- Whether ld+json vehicle blobs are present and stable.
- The CSS selectors and interaction pattern needed to perform a keyword search.
- A JSON sample of at least 5 parsed vehicle objects with the key fields above.
- Notes on what filters appear to be controllable via URL vs only via UI.
experiments.summary: Confirmed that Carvana SRP exposes one application/ld+json[data-qa='vehicle-ld'] per vehicle and that we can trigger keyword searches via the search input and scrape rich vehicle data (VIN, price, URL) from these blobs without calling blocked APIs.

output.ld_json_vehicle_blobs_notes: On the SRP at https://www.carvana.com/cars there are multiple <script type="application/ld+json" data-qa="vehicle-ld"> tags, one per vehicle tile. These are present both in captured snapshots and in the live page after performing a search. Live extraction after a search returned 21 Vehicle objects. Structure matches the captured SUV SRP snapshot: schema.org Vehicle with nested Offer.

search_ui_selectors.interaction_pattern: Focus the input, set value, dispatch an 'input' event, then dispatch Enter keydown/keyup to trigger search. Example JS: const input=document.querySelector('input[name="search"].Search-module_input__M-8ku__v4_2_2'); input.focus(); input.value='audi'; input.dispatchEvent(new Event('input',{bubbles:true})); input.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent('keydown',{key:'Enter',code:'Enter',which:13,keyCode:13,bubbles:true})); input.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent('keyup',{key:'Enter',code:'Enter',which:13,keyCode:13,bubbles:true}));

url_observations: Base SRP URL after live search remained https://www.carvana.com/cars with an empty query string (no ?make=, ?model=, etc.).
Captured SUV SRP uses path-based body style filter: https://www.carvana.com/cars/suv (with optional ?refSource=...).

App-router internal data shows filters encoded in a filters segment in the route: /(carvana-layout)/cars/[[...filters]] with examples like ["filters","suv","oc"]. This indicates filters such as body style are primarily path-based, not query-based.
ui_only_or_internal_filters: Other facets (price range, monthly payment, down payment, drivetrain, etc.) appear as inputs and checkboxes in the DOM and are reflected in React/Next internal state (AppliedFiltersContext) but are not exposed as simple URL query params on the live SRP URL.
Filter state (bodyStyles, etc.) is present in server-provided JSON/React context and in internal links SEO blocks, not as plain query parameters.

output.conclusion: Using only the public SRP UI, it is feasible to reliably trigger keyword searches by programmatically interacting with the search box (input[name="search"].Search-module_input__M-8ku__v4_2_2) and then scraping structured vehicle data from the application/ld+json[data-qa="vehicle-ld"] scripts. Each vehicle tile has a stable ld+json blob with name, model year, VIN, SKU, mileageFromOdometer, price, currency, and canonical vehicle URL. Body-style filters are encoded in the path (e.g., /cars/suv) and additional facets are managed via internal state/checkboxes rather than obvious URL query parameters, so deeper filter control will require simulating UI interactions rather than constructing query strings.

experiments.hypothesis: Carvana vehicle details for a specific vehicleId can be obtained without calling blocked apim.carvana.io APIs by scraping structured data from the public VDP HTML (ld+json Vehicle schema and Next.js __NEXT_DATA__).
experiments.rationale: Network exploration shows apim.carvana.io/vehicle-details-api is blocked by Cloudflare, but DOM exploration indicates the VDP exposes rich structured data: an application/ld+json Vehicle blob plus a __NEXT_DATA__ script with vehicleId, pricing, specs, and context. If these are stable on the live site, we can build carvana_get_vehicle_details as a pure HTML/JS scraping routine instead of direct API calls.
experiments.prompt:
Goal: Verify that a Carvana vehicle details page for a known vehicleId exposes enough structured data in HTML/JS to build a robust get_vehicle_details routine without direct API calls.

Target vehicleId: 4195259 (from exploration summaries).

Steps (use tools by name):
1) Use browser_navigate to go to https://www.carvana.com/vehicle/4195259.
2) After the page loads and any Cloudflare challenge passes, use browser_get_dom to confirm you're on a VDP (look for elements like data-qa="vehicle-title" or price components).
3) Use browser_get_dom or browser_eval_js to locate:
   - The <script type="application/ld+json" data-qa="vehicle-ld"> in the head/body.
   - The main __NEXT_DATA__ script tag (id="__NEXT_DATA__" if present) or App Router flight data scripts (self.__next_f pushes).
4) Use browser_eval_js to:
   a) Parse the application/ld+json[data-qa="vehicle-ld"] into a JSON object.
   b) Parse window.__NEXT_DATA__ (if present) or the relevant App Router data structure to extract a structured vehicle object including: vehicleId, vin, sku, year/model/trim, mileage, main price, priceCurrency, main image URL(s), and canonical VDP URL.
5) Return a JSON object with:
   - ld_json_vehicle: the parsed Vehicle schema object.
   - next_data_vehicle: the parsed vehicle details from __NEXT_DATA__ or App Router data, with at least the fields above.
   - notes on stability: e.g., whether keys/paths look stable, any obvious feature flags, and whether Cloudflare interfered.

Output:
- Confirm whether we can implement carvana_get_vehicle_details by scraping HTML/JS only.
- Provide exact JS property paths used to extract the key fields so we can hardcode them in a routine later.
experiments.summary: Confirmed that Carvana VDP exposes detailed vehicle data in window.__NEXT_DATA__.props.pageProps.forProviders.forVehicleContext.vehicleDetails for a known vehicleId, so we can build get_vehicle_details as a pure HTML/JS scraping routine without direct APIs.

notes.stability_assessment: Vehicle details are embedded in window.__NEXT_DATA__ under props.pageProps.forProviders.forVehicleContext.vehicleDetails. Keys like vehicleId, vin, year, make, model, trim, mileage, price, msrp, inventoryType look domain-specific and stable. No application/ld+json[data-qa="vehicle-ld"] was present on this page. Cloudflare did not block access in this run.

experiments.hypothesis: Alternative Carvana SRP search flow can be automated with simpler, non-conditional URL templating and still yield ld+json vehicle data for a fixed body style.
experiments.rationale: The first experiment proved ld+json scraping works for /cars, but routine construction got stuck on conditional body-style handling. We can instead treat body style as non-parameterized and hardcode a specific SRP path (e.g., /cars) to keep the routine schema simple while still satisfying "search by model/type" via keyword.
experiments.prompt:
Goal: Validate that using only the base SRP at https://www.carvana.com/cars (no body-style path parameterization) plus keyword search is sufficient to retrieve diverse vehicles and their ld+json blobs.

Steps (use tools by name):
1) Use browser_navigate to go to https://www.carvana.com/cars.
2) Use browser_eval_js to run a search for the keyword 'audi' exactly as in experiment 3d9zgt (focus input[name="search"], set value, dispatch input + Enter key events).
3) After results load, use browser_eval_js to collect and JSON.parse all application/ld+json[data-qa="vehicle-ld"] scripts into an array.
4) Return a compact JSON object with: count, and an array of up to 10 vehicles including name, modelDate, vehicleIdentificationNumber, sku, mileageFromOdometer, offers.price, offers.priceCurrency, and url.

Output:
- Confirmation that base /cars SRP without a body-style segment still returns rich ld+json for a keyword search.
- Sample vehicles showing that make/model filtering via keyword works without path parameters.
experiments.summary: Confirmed that using the base /cars SRP plus a keyword search reliably returns multiple ld+json Vehicle blobs, so a search routine can ignore body-style path parameters and still provide rich inventory data.

output.summary: Validated that the base /cars SRP with a keyword search returns rich ld+json vehicle data.
output.confirmation: Base https://www.carvana.com/cars SRP, with only a keyword search for 'audi' and no body-style path segment, returned 21 application/ld+json[data-qa='vehicle-ld'] scripts. catalog.usage_guide:
There are two shipped Carvana routines:

1) carvana_search_inventory
   - What it does: Navigates to the public Carvana /cars search results page, performs a keyword search in the built-in search box, and scrapes structured Vehicle ld+json blobs for all vehicles currently shown.
   - Inputs: `search_query` (string) — a keyword such as a make, model, or general term (e.g., "audi", "tesla", "suv").
   - Output: An object with `count` and `vehicles[]`, where each vehicle includes name, model year, VIN, SKU, mileageFromOdometer, an `offers` object (price, priceCurrency, availability, canonical vehicle URL), and a top-level `url` pointing to the VDP.
   - When to use: Whenever you need to find cars for sale on Carvana by free-text search and get a list of matching vehicles with VINs, prices, and links, without touching Carvana’s internal APIs. Use this first to discover interesting vehicles and capture their `vehicleId` from the URL.

2) carvana_get_vehicle_details
   - What it does: Navigates directly to a specific Carvana vehicle details page (VDP) using a known `vehicleId` and extracts rich structured data from `window.__NEXT_DATA__.props.pageProps.forProviders.forVehicleContext.vehicleDetails`.
   - Inputs: `vehicle_id` (integer) — the Carvana internal ID from the VDP URL path `/vehicle/{vehicleId}`. Obtain it from `carvana_search_inventory` results (parse the numeric ID from each `url`) or by copying from a VDP URL.
   - Output: A structured object with core identity fields (vehicleId, VIN, SKU, year, make, model, trim), usage info (mileage), pricing (price, priceCurrency, MSRP), inventory metadata (inventoryType), main image URL, canonical URL, and a `raw` sub-object containing many additional specs, features, warranty, location, and media details.
   - When to use: After you know exactly which Carvana vehicle you care about and need deep details beyond what the SRP exposes.

How to use them together:
- Step 1: Call `carvana_search_inventory` with an appropriate `search_query` (e.g., a make+model) to get a list of matching vehicles. Inspect the returned `vehicles` array and pick one or more candidates by their `url`.
- Step 2: Extract the numeric `vehicleId` from each chosen `url` (it’s the path segment after `/vehicle/`).
- Step 3: For each chosen ID, call `carvana_get_vehicle_details` with `vehicle_id` to retrieve a comprehensive details payload suitable for downstream analysis, comparison, or display.

Notes:
- Both routines work entirely via public HTML/JS scraping, so they avoid Cloudflare-blocked internal APIs.
- Neither routine currently parameterizes advanced filters (price range, drivetrain, etc.); to approximate those, encode them into your `search_query` (e.g., "audi q8"), then post-filter the returned results client-side.
- If a given `vehicle_id` is invalid or no longer available, `carvana_get_vehicle_details` will return an error field like `vehicle_details_missing` from its js_evaluate step; callers should be prepared to handle null/empty results.
